evaluations.query: visually-rich document understanding model for layout-aware retrieval over scanned PDFs — jointly encodes OCR text, spatial positions, and page images
evaluations.reason: None include GT vidore/colpali. Method B excels with QwenAmann-4B-dse at #1 (document-level visually-rich retrieval), layoutlmv3 at #2 (the canonical layout-aware encoder jointly modeling text, spatial positions, and images), and PaddleOCR-VL at #3. Method C has layoutlmv3 at #1 (directly matching the query's 'jointly encodes OCR text, spatial positions, and page images') but Gliese-OCR and dots.ocr are pure OCR. Method A is entirely OCR-focused with no retrieval or layout-aware encoding capability.

evaluations.query: high-fidelity text-to-image diffusion model with strong text rendering capability and compositional scene control
evaluations.reason: Method A has GT stable-diffusion-3.5-large at #2 (SD3.5 uses rectified flow with triple text encoders for superior text rendering), Qwen-Image at #1, and HunyuanImage-3.0 at #3 — all capable of compositional scene control. Method C has kandinsky-3 and HunyuanImage-2.1 — decent diffusion models but neither is known for strong text rendering. Method B has QwenImage-Rebalance (a fine-tune, not a standalone model), HunyuanImage-2.1, and Ming-flash-omni (multimodal, not text-to-image) — poor fit for the compositional generation query.

evaluations.query: real-time monocular depth estimation network optimized for robotics, metric depth output from single RGB frame without auxiliary sensors
evaluations.reason: Methods B and C are identical: DepthPro-hf/#1 or apple/DepthPro/#1, and critically Depth-Anything-V2-Metric-Indoor-Small-hf at #3 — which outputs metric depth (not relative), directly matching the robotics requirement for absolute distance. Method B has DepthPro (non-hf) at #1, GT-adjacent at #2, metric model at #3. Method A has marigold-normals at #3 (surface normal estimation, not depth) — a miss for a query explicitly requesting metric depth.

evaluations.query: large multimodal model supporting interleaved image/video understanding, multi-language OCR, UI screenshot comprehension, and visual question answering
evaluations.reason: None include the exact GT Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking. Method B recommends Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking (same family, larger, with thinking capability), InternVL3_5-241B, and Qwen3-Omni — all flagship VLMs supporting interleaved image/video, OCR, and UI comprehension. Method C has InternVL3-8B and InternVL3_5 variants — strong VLMs but all from one family, less diversity. Method A has UniMedVL (medical-domain, not general UI) at #1 and small Qwen3-VL GGUF quantizations at #2/#3 — less suitable for a 'large' model query.

evaluations.query: multi-label emotion classification transformer fine-tuned on GoEmotions or similar dataset, outputs probability distribution over co-occurring emotion categories
evaluations.reason: Method B has GT roberta-base-go_emotions at #1 (explicitly multi-label, trained on GoEmotions with 28 emotion categories), EmoRoBERTa at #2 (also GoEmotions-based), and bert-base-emotion at #3. Method C has emotion_text_classifier, emotion-distilroberta, and bert-base-emotion — relevant emotion classifiers but none specifically multi-label GoEmotions. Method A has emotion_text_classifier and EmoRoBERTa but speech-emotion-recognition at #3 is audio-based, not text — a notable miss for a text classification query.

evaluations.query: multilingual hybrid retrieval embedding model with both dense vector and learned sparse representations, supporting long-document chunking across 100+ languages
evaluations.reason: All three have GT bge-m3 at #1 (which natively supports dense, sparse, and multi-vector retrieval across 100+ languages). Method A adds nomic-embed-v2-moe (multilingual MoE embeddings) and splade-v3 (learned sparse retrieval) — directly addressing the hybrid dense+sparse requirement. Method C has nomic-embed-v2-moe and nvidia/llama-nv-embedqa (dense only). Method B has nvidia/llama-nv-embedqa and gte-multilingual — both dense-only models, not addressing the sparse retrieval aspect.
